To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the single-particle potentials for nucleons in neutron-rich nuclear matter are strongly isospin- (and momentum-) dependent, and the momentum dependence of these potentials is crucial for describing intermediate-energy heavy-ion reaction dynamics and for understanding the structure and stability of neutron stars.

(i) the single-particle potentials in neutron-rich matter depend on the density and the isospin asymmetries, the momentum and isovin of the particle as well as the temperature of the medium, and (ii) these dependencies are essential for a quantitative understanding of the dynamics of intermediate-energy heavy-ion reactions and the thermal and mechanical properties of neutron stars
the isospin- (or isovector) and momentum-dependent interactions are important for understanding the isospin dynamics in intermediate-energy heavy-ion reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of asymmetric nuclear systems, including the equation of state, the single-particle potentials and the thermal properties.

the study of the properties of nuclear matter and neutron stars, and the development of new nuclear interactions and effective models for the description of nuclear systems at finite temperature and density.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the momentum dependence of both isovector and isoscalar potentials is essential for a realistic description of neutron-rich matter.

the momentum-dependent Gogny-type interactions, in general, give a reasonable description of the nuclear many-body system, and that the isovector momentum dependence of the interaction is important for the description of nuclear properties.
the momentum-dependent Gogny-type interaction provides a good tool to probe the isospin- as well as momentum-dependent nuclear effective interaction in neutron-rich matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gogny-type interactions are capable to describe a wide range of properties of asymmetric nuclear and hyperonic matter.

a Gogny interaction with isospin- but not momentum-dependent terms is insufficient for studying neutron-rich matter, and a Gogny type interaction with momentum-dependent terms but without isospin dependence would not be sufficient for studying neutron-rich asymmetric matter.

a Gogny-like isospin- as well as momentum-dependent interaction is a good choice in studying the properties of nuclear matter in the intermediate-energy heavy-ion reactions, in the thermal properties of neutron-rich matter and the properties of neutron stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the isospin- (and momentum-) dependent effective interaction is crucial to understand the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies and the properties of neutron stars, in particular, the neutron star maximum mass.
the isovector momentum dependence of the nuclear interaction plays a key role in the description of the isospinning properties of asymmetric nuclear systems.

the isospin- (or density) and momentum-dependent nuclear interactions, which have been used extensively in the literature for the last 20 years or so, are not unique and that the isospine and momentum dependence of nuclear interactions can be modified in many different ways to fit the same experimental or theoretical data.
